--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_match()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the nodes or edges that match a Cypher MATCH pattern. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_match()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the nodes or edges that match a Cypher MATCH pattern. title: >- [Graph.select_match()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select the nodes or edges that match a Cypher MATCH pattern. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select the nodes or edges that match a Cypher `MATCH` pattern. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25284-L25500){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_match( query, select=None, params=None, set_op="union", distinct_nodes=False, label_key="name", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select the matches of a pattern](../assets/graphs/select-match.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed six-node grid A to F with no selection, where B and C point at each other and so do D and E. After select_match with MATCH (a)-->(b)-->(a), every node in a 2-cycle is selected: B, C, D, and E, in the accent color. A and F are in no cycle and stay plain." width="100%"} Finds every match of the pattern, as `match()` does, and selects what the matches bound: every node of every match, or only the variables that `select=` names. The selection then feeds the `*_ws` methods, so a query can tag, recolor or extract the parts of the graph that fit a pattern. The query is the same as for `match()` (see there for the supported Cypher and how it reads the graph), except that it can't have a `RETURN` clause, since `select=` chooses what to keep. A graph holds a selection of nodes or a selection of edges, never both, so `select=` names one kind: - `select=None` (the default) selects every node in any match, including the anonymous ones in patterns such as `(p)-->()` and the nodes along variable-length paths. That highlights every occurrence of the pattern. - `select="p"` or `select=["p", "q"]` selects only the nodes those variables matched. - A path variable counts as a node variable, and selects every node on its paths. - Relationship variables, as in `select="r"`, select edges instead. A variable-length one selects every edge on its paths. - After `WITH`, the matches are those of the last part, and `select=` names its variables: those it matches and the columns of the `WITH` before it that hold nodes or relationships. `select=None` selects the nodes of the last part's matches, which include the nodes that `WITH` passes on, but not the ones that earlier parts matched and `WITH` dropped. A variable that an `OPTIONAL MATCH` left `null` selects nothing. A selection loses the pairing within each match: after selecting `a` and `b` from `(a)-[:KNOWS]->(b)`, you can't tell who knows whom. `match()` keeps the pairs. The selection combines with the current one according to `set_op=`, like the other `select_*` methods. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [query]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Cypher text, such as `"MATCH (p:Person)-[:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie)"`. Anything outside the supported subset raises a `ValueError` that gives the line and column. [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Union[str, list[str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : What to select: `None` (the default) for every node of every match, or the name of a variable, or a list of names. The names must all be node (or path) variables or all be relationship variables, and can't be columns of `WITH` that hold other values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[dict]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Values for the `$name` parameters in the query, as a dict such as `{"year": 1999}`. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How the matches combine with the current selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected elements among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any selection of the other kind (edges when selecting nodes, and nodes when selecting edges) is cleared. [distinct_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, the nodes of a match must all be different, as in a subgraph isomorphism. The default follows Cypher, where only the edges must differ. [label_key]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["name"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The property that reads the node label when a node has no attribute of that name (`"name"` by default, matching `from_cypher()`), or `None` to read only attributes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the query is invalid (as for `match()`) or has a `RETURN` clause; if `select=` names a variable that the query doesn't bind or that holds a value, or mixes node and relationship variables; or if `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. The selection is left unchanged. [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `query=` isn't a string, `select=` isn't a name or a list of names, `params=` isn't a dict, or `label_key=` isn't a string or `None`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The movie graph from `match()`, with three people and two movies: ::: {#e2046994 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.from_cypher(""" CREATE (keanu:Person {name: 'Keanu Reeves', born: 1964}), (carrie:Person {name: 'Carrie-Anne Moss', born: 1967}), (lana:Person {name: 'Lana Wachowski', born: 1965}), (matrix:Movie {title: 'The Matrix', released: 1999}), (wick:Movie {title: 'John Wick', released: 2014}), (keanu)-[:ACTED_IN {roles: ['Neo']}]->(matrix), (carrie)-[:ACTED_IN {roles: ['Trinity']}]->(matrix), (keanu)-[:ACTED_IN {roles: ['John Wick']}]->(wick), (lana)-[:DIRECTED]->(matrix) """) ``` ::: Selecting the people who acted in a movie, and tagging them: ::: {#401abb49 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .select_match("MATCH (p:Person)-[:ACTED_IN]->(:Movie)", select="p") .set_node_attrs_ws(actor=True) .get_node_df() .select("label", "actor") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 2)
labelactor
strbool
"Keanu Reeves"true
"Carrie-Anne Moss"true
"Lana Wachowski"null
"matrix"null
"wick"null
``` ::: ::: Without `select=`, every node of every match is selected, which for this pattern is everyone connected to The Matrix, and the movie itself: ::: {#79821481 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_match( "MATCH (m:Movie {title: $title})--(p)", params={"title": "The Matrix"}, set_op="replace", ) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(i) for i in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['Carrie-Anne Moss', 'Keanu Reeves', 'Lana Wachowski', 'matrix'] ``` ::: ::: A relationship variable selects edges. Here, the acting credits in movies released after 2000: ::: {#d72086be .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_match( "MATCH (:Person)-[r:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie) WHERE m.released > 2000", select="r" ) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
